title: No query_execution knob change is justified: GetUserTweets terminal saturation is structural (fully cached, index-driven read path), not a planner/executor misconfiguration
configuration_cause: None attributable to any allowed query_execution knob. The incumbent plan evidence is an Index Scan with estimated_rows=1.0 and estimated_total_cost=8.45, i.e. the planner already picks the only sensible access path; the read side is fully cache-resident (buffer_hit_ratio 0.9999265, blks_read 20.1/s, blks_hit 273328/s) with seq_scan=0.0/s, temp_files=0.0/s, temp_bytes=0.0, deadlocks=0.0/s and lock_waiting_backends 0 at every percentile, so there is no observable mis-estimation, spill, or lock stall for default_statistics_target / random_page_cost / seq_page_cost / work_mem / jit / parallelism to correct.
mechanism: Closed-loop terminal-budget identity: goodput_rps ~= terminals / weighted-mean client latency = 8 / 283us ~= 28.3k rps, which reproduces the measured 28257 rps. GetUserTweets is ~90% of the transaction mix (3048834 of ~3.4M transactions) at a 169us p50 / 278us mean on a fully cached index path (9.67 buffer hits/txn, 7.27 tuples fetched/txn, blk_read_time 7.2e-6 ms/txn, zero temp bytes), so it owns 0.884 of the finite 8-terminal budget. That cost is per-query executor CPU on hot shared buffers plus the client round trip; the statement never enqueues on the WAL commit path (wal_write_per_txn 0.0075, wal_bytes_per_txn 5.17B) and never waits on a lock. Consequently no knob in the query_execution set changes the dominant term: the tail (p99 2813us) has no accompanying I/O, lock, or WAL signal to attribute it to.
query_effect: GetUserTweets performs an index access returning ~7 rows per transaction entirely from shared buffers; no sequential scans, no sorts or temp spills, no heap-read stalls and no lock acquisition beyond instantaneous buffer pins. Its latency is fixed per-query planner+executor CPU plus client round trip, which none of the allowed planner/statistics/executor knobs reduce without an observable defect to correct.
expected_tps_effect: unchanged within +/-5% of the incumbent band 29762.6-31906.7 rps (median 30213.6); the 28257 rps observation is a low draw of the same configuration, not a configuration regression.
expected_latency_effect: unchanged; GetUserTweets p50 ~169us and overall p95 ~754us stay within the observed replicate spread (baseline p50 157-169us, p95 646-696us).

predictions.rationale: Closed-loop identity 8 terminals / 283us mean = 28.3k rps matches the measured 28257 rps. With knob_changes=[] the configuration is bit-identical to the incumbent, so throughput must stay within +/-5% of the 29762.6-31906.7 rps replicate band; the current 28257 rps is inside the run-to-run spread already seen across baseline_1..3 (7% band).

0.8838 = 848.4s of 960s of terminal time at ~3.05M transactions; baselines were 0.8798/0.8817/0.8787. With identical config, count (~3.05M) and mean latency (278us) are unchanged, so the fraction stays ~0.88 within +/-5%; no query_execution knob alters transaction frequency or the cached-read mean.

p50 169us is a shared-buffer index access (0.9999265 hit ratio, 9.67 blks_hit/txn, 7.2e-6 ms blk_read_time/txn, 0 temp bytes). No allowed knob changes the executor path for this Index Scan (est_rows 1.0, est_cost 8.45); baseline p50s were 165/169/157us (+/-4%), so a 10% tolerance is conservative.

Measured WAL write average 0.138ms with host_io some/full stall fraction 0.0, wal_sync=0.0/s and wal_sync_time_per_txn=0.0; the wal_wait alert rests on one instantaneous sample (wal_waiting_backends median 0, p95 0, max 1 of ~9 backends) and on 5.17 WAL bytes/txn. A genuine WAL-stall mechanism would need order-of-magnitude higher write latency or sustained waiters, so the mean stays within +/-0.5ms.

alternatives.statement: GetUserTweets latency is partly planner-induced (a mis-estimated or heap-fetch-heavy plan) that a cost-constant / statistics-target change could shorten; the supplied plan_evidence only covers the trivial probe (id=1) and not the real GetUserTweets SQL.
The 28257 rps observation is simply a low draw of the unchanged configuration and would recover to the 29762-31907 rps band on a repeat with no knob change.
The wal_wait alert is real but affects only the single-table writer path (InsertTweet) via rare WAL flush grouping, leaving the read-dominant GetUserTweets untouched.

cross_domain_requirements: concurrency_maintenance: attribute the GetUserTweets p99 (2813us) and max (30888us) tail to LWLock/buffer-pin wait or CPU scheduling, since lock_waiting_backends=0 and locks_waiting=0 at all percentiles.

memory_storage: confirm whether the wal_wait alert is a single-sample artifact (wal_waiting_backends p95=0, host_io stalls 0.0, write_average_ms 0.138) and whether any commit-path change is justified.
why_exceeds_incumbent: It does not exceed the incumbent; the incumbent is already at the terminal-budget ceiling for this transaction mix. Because seq_scan=0.0/s, temp_bytes=0, deadlocks=0, lock_waiting_backends=0 and buffer_hit_ratio=0.9999265, there is no observable planner/executor defect for any allowed query_execution knob (default_statistics_target, random_page_cost, seq_page_cost, effective_cache_size, work_mem, jit, from/join_collapse_limit, max_parallel_workers_per_gather) to correct. Applying an un-evidenced planner change would only add regression risk to a healthy, guardrail-passing incumbent.
